newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan urges restraint after U.S. strike on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan urges restraint after U.S. strike on Iraq.

text.p: Pakistan voiced extreme concern on Tuesday at U.S. missile strikes on Iraq and urged all sides to show restraint to avoid worsening tension in the region.
"Pakistan is following with extreme concern the news that the United States has launched cruise missile strikes against selected air defence targets in Iraq," a Foreign Ministry statement said.
"Pakistan feels that resort to use of force by any side will only exacerbate the existing tensions posing fresh dangers to peace in the region," it said.

"Pakistan reiterates its support for the territorial integrity and sovereignty of Iraq, and the inviolability of its borders. It strongly urges all sides to exercise the greatest restraint and calls upon them to strictly adhere to the United Nations resolutions pertaining to Iraq," the statement added.

Islamic Pakistan, which has been trying to improve its previously strained relations with the United States, sent troops to Saudi Arabia to join the allied coalition against Iraq during the 1990-91 Gulf crisis.
Popular opinion at the time, however, strongly favoured Iraqi President Saddam Hussein.
Pakistan has since sent food and other humanitarian assistance to Iraq to alleviate the impact of U.N. sanctions.

"The government and people of Pakistan have time and again expressed their deepest sympathy for the people of Iraq, who have been the principal victims of the unfortunate situation," the Foreign Ministry statement said.
Former Pakistan cricket captain Imran Khan, who now leads a political party called Tehreek-i-Insaaf (Justice Movement), condemned the American attack on Iraq.
He said in a statement that the U.S. action lacked the support of the U.N. Security Council and did not advance the cause of peace in the region.

"In fact the attack violated (U.N. Security Council) resolution 688 which reaffirms the commitment of all member states to respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of Iraq," the statement said.
